chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Coleman Hawkins's "Body and Soul" and selling it in Boston
summary: McRae recalls Hawkins's letter and buys 500 copies for Harvard students while Hawkins was in Europe; Welburn corrects the dating.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Because Coleman say -- I understand somebody said to me that -- I got a letter from Coleman Hawkins. Coleman say, 'You guys say everybody say (inaudible) he's going back. But he's going to send you a little message to let you know that he's not going back,' you know. They figured Coleman had been in Europe and he had lost, you know, (inaudible) -- not where they get that idea. playing good, (inaudible). So they released 'Body and Soul' over here. That's when Chuck Berry was on his high horse. He was like, oh man, I'm the greatest, you know -- with Cab -- I'm the greatest, you know.

Playing with Chick Webb there.
(Inaudible) picture him and Chick walking out the Savoy together. I say, yeah, (inaudible) Ch Berry.
Then he went with Cab. But at that time -- this particular time was the most funny thing, you know, so (inaudible) because I know at that time that --
When I got this letter from Coleman Hawkins, he said -- they tell me that --
There's a tall guy out there -- they say I'm going back. That means I'm not playing as good as I -- you know.
He says, but I got news. I'm going to send you a little letter. That's when he made 'Body and Soul'.
He (Inaudible) made it before he left here, they just released it. They made up their mind to release it.
Because I was in Boston with Chick. I come down and went to the Commodore and said, 'Give me 500 of (Inaudible) the records.'
Because the college kids used to hang out

over Mother's Lunch. I was staying there and I had all the jazz records, and they came over there.
You know, guys from Harvard -- they used to come over there, you know. Especially this nephew of Bethlehem Steel -- he used to hang out with me all the time.
So, I went and got these records. They were selling them like for five dollars a piece. They bought them -- say, 'Go down and get some more.' I went down and got some more.
And they all lasted one day. Everybody in school wanted 'Body and Soul', you know.
And when the record hit the thing -- when we came on, it hit the air here, everybody came back, they were playing -- trying to play Coleman Hawkins' 'Body and Soul'. Everybody jumped on it.
And, boy, there was a lot of red faces around there. Coleman Hawkins was still in Europe. So the winter of '37 -- (inaudible) '37 --
He came back just before

Some time in '39, I think he'd just gotten back and recorded. He may have gone back after he recorded --
No, he didn't go back.
Well he recorded it in New York. All the (inaudible) documentation points to his recording in New York. And then they may have released it first in Europe,, and then released over here.
I think they did release it first in Europe, because he was in Europe when they released that, because it came back. It was a (inaudible) lot of excitement. When he came back, that record was --
Red hot.
Red hot for him, you know. The talk of the whole country, that 'Body and Soul.'
